policy.uncertifiedDefault: Any sugya absent from records is UNCERTIFIED, regardless of legacy review metadata or historical audit findings.
policy.certification: CERTIFIED requires fresh sourceFingerprint and semanticFingerprint plus two fingerprint-bound source-first reviews with different reviewId values.
policy.repairProof: A first pass that finds REPAIR_REQUIRED cannot certify until repairRef exists and the live candidate differs from the first-pass reviewed fingerprints.
policy.invalidation: Any source, boundary, mapping, daf-summary, or semantic fingerprint change automatically makes the prior certificate STALE.
policy.bootstrapExit: Set strictMode true only after validate_semantic_certification.py --strict passes across the full corpus.

evidence.summary: Independent reconstruction of the whole daf (Mishnah lines 1-7; Gemara lines 8-39, ending mid-word at 've'eima') confirms this sugya's speaker attributions, sourceRefs, and scope are all correct with no fabrication, reversed attribution, or false closure.

Mutually-blind independent reconstruction of all 39 raw Hebrew lines, re-verifying all six sugyot's sourceRefs, speaker attributions (Rabbi Yehuda/Sages, tvul-yom/Sadducees, Rabbi Yochanan/Reish Lakish on bira), the asymmetric elimination argument at lines 32-34, and the honest unresolved 've'eima' cutoff at line 39. No defect found in any of the six sugyot.

fieldInventory.note: case: line 1 states the base rule (seven-day separation, backup priest) as a given case, not a proof/rejection.
proposal: line 4 is Rabbi Yehuda's affirmative extension proposing a backup wife.
rejection: lines 6-7 are the Sages' formal 'ein la'davar sof' rejection of the proposal.
intro: opening Mishnah, no prior sugya context required.
logical: the sugya turns on an infinite-regress objection, a logical rather than textual/hermeneutical move.
logical_principle: the takeaway states a general principle about bounding contingency-chains, not a halachic ruling or terminology point.

confirmedDefects.dafLevel.summary / yoma-004b-s02: The baraita's 'given on the 7th' position is authored by a sage named plain 'Rabbi Yosi' (line 13, distinct from 'Rabbi Yosi HaGalili'); R. Akiva's alignment with that view is a separate, later Gemara statement (line 21, 'R. Akiva holds like Rabbi Yosi'). Round-1 wording glossed over this, risking the impression the baraita itself names R. Akiva for the 7th-day view.
confirmedDefects.yoma-004b-s02 step-05 (round-1 repair er: Round-1 repair introduced an unsupported claim that 'the verse doubles Moses's name' as the derash mechanism for R. Elazar's honor-reading. The bracketed '[Moshe]' in line 1 and the repeated 'Moshe Moshe' in line 27 are the Gemara's own citation/paraphrase style, not a Torah-text name-doubling derash; Rashi's comment on this point (lines 4-5) grounds the honor-derash in the public context (Israel standing by), never in name-repetition. No name-doubling derash (of the classic 'Avraham Avraham' type) is attested in the source or Rashi for this line.
confirmedDefects.yoma-004b-s03 step-06 (round-1 repair er: Round-1 repair introduced an attribution to 'Rav Mesharshiya' as an alternate name for this teaching's author. This name does not appear anywhere in this daf's raw text or bundled Rashi. The source's actual bracketed alternate attribution (line 39) is a different, genuinely obscure name ('R. Musia the son of the son of R. Msia, in the name of R. Musia'); 'Rav Mesharshiya' appears to have been mistakenly carried over from an unrelated attribution on daf 2b.

evidence.summary: Fresh, isolated Source Auditor first-pass audit of Yoma 5b (yoma-005b-s01, yoma-005b-s02), independently reconstructed from rawHebrewLines and relevantRashi without trusting existing enrichment.
evidence.majorFindings: dafLevel.summary and s01's display/learning/argumentFlow narrative wrongly present the baraita (lines 5-9) as a direct continuation of the inauguration-passage indispensability bridge-building (steps 1-4, Lev. 8:35). Independently re-verified against relevantRashi on line 5: Rashi states explicitly this baraita's phrases are 'not that same verse belonging to the inauguration passage... but rather [the one] regarding the eighth day' (Lev. 10:12ff, the Nadav-and-Avihu aftermath). The shared 'ki chen tzuviti' wording is a coincidental phrase-match, not a substantive continuation. The dafLevel glossary's Aninus entry compounds this by stating the inauguration itself occurred while Nadav and Avihu had just died, when in fact they died on the eighth day, immediately after the inauguration concluded.
mediumFindings: s01 argumentFlow step-06 conflates two separate derivation mechanisms: trousers via the inclusive 've-zeh hadavar' vav, and the tenth-ephah via a distinct gezerah shavah on 'zeh'/'zeh' to Lev. 6:13 (already correctly separated in step-07). Text incorrectly implies both derive from the same mechanism.

dafLevel glossary's gezerah shavah entry omits the 'yeteira' (redundant repetition) requirement that licenses the petach analogy, confirmed present in Rashi's own gloss on line 2 ('redundantly, and likewise in the performance').
s01 lineRange.endVilnaLine declared 15, but step-08's own proof-text and conclusion run through line 18 ('ת''ל ויאמר משה אל העדה זה הדבר אשר צוה ה' אפילו דיבור מעכב'), an unaccounted boundary gap.

s02 argumentFlow step-03 telegraphs Abaye's belt-only narrowing ('(for the belt)') before the Gemara itself supplies it at step-04; at that point in the raw text (lines 22-25) the R. Chiyya's-sons/R. Yochanan dispute is stated in fully general terms.
minorFindings: s01/s02 topicTags contain capitalized non-slug values ('Leviticus', 'Moses', 'Abaye') violating the lowercase-hyphen-ASCII-slug contract.
s01/s02 requiresUnderstanding hold prose sentences instead of sugya ids, violating the contract (prose belongs in prerequisiteKnowledge).
s01/s02 visualizableElements use legacy 'description' key instead of the canonical required 'item' field.
noDefectsConfirmed: No cross-sugya lineId citations (all sourceRefs resolve within their own sugya's segment map).
s02's finalRuling correctly null; the belt-sequence stub is correctly framed as open, not resolved, with Rashi's own note confirming the answer continues on 6a.
Verse attributions in s02 step-05 (Lev. 8:7/8:13, Exod. 29:9) match Rashi's citations exactly.

evidence.reconstruction: Independent second-pass review, mutually-blind from the round-1 repair context (a6749807a314bfcfe). Reconstructed the whole daf from rawHebrewLines and relevantRashi: (1-4) three Amoraic bridges from Exodus-inauguration kachah to Leviticus requirements (petach-petach gezerah shavah, mishmeret-Hashem inclusivity, ki-chen-tzuviti warrant); (5-9) the eighth-day baraita distinguishing three near-identical phrases; (9-15) trousers and tenth-of-ephah derivations plus R. Yochanan's mikra-parasha point; (19-34) the dressing-order question, Abaye's belt-only narrowing, verse-proofs, and the unresolved challenge cut off mid-word at line 34.
evidence.attributionCheck: Verified against Rashi line by line: petach redundancy, mishmeret-Hashem inclusivity, the three ki-chen phrases' distinct referents, trousers/tenth-of-ephah sourcing, Abaye's belt-only narrowing, the verse-proofs and the reversed challenge. All match.
evidence.boundaryAndSourceRefCheck: Every argumentFlow step's lineId is one of its own sugya's sourceSegmentMap mintedLineIds, and every vilnaLine falls within that segment's declared containment range. No cross-sugya or cross-daf leakage; nothing from 6a is imported.
evidence.fabricationCheck: No fabrication found. The davar/dibbur gloss for R. Yochanan's derivation is directly supported by the Gemara's own adjacent wording (apilu dibbur me'akev), not invented.
evidence.closureCheck: finalRuling is null for both sugyot; s02's learning.resolution explicitly states the resolution is left for 6a. No misattributed closure.
evidence.majorFindingReverification: The line 5-9 baraita is correctly framed throughout (dafLevel.summary, s01 shortSummary/whats, step-05, note field) as belonging to the eighth-day/Nadav-Avihu passage (Lev. 10), appended only for shared ki-chen-tzuviti wording with Rav Ashi's proof, matching Rashi's own comment on line 5 verbatim. Trousers and tenth-of-ephah are correctly presented as two distinct mechanisms, matching Rashi's bishlama/ela structure. s02 step-03 describes the initial dispute with no premature mention of the belt; step-04 (Abaye) is where the belt-only scope is first introduced.
evidence.overallVerdict: No defects found in display, learning, argumentFlow, misconceptions, quizSeeds, glossary, or topicTags fields for either sugya.

evidence.summary: Fresh, isolated Source Auditor first-pass audit of Yoma 5b (yoma-005b-s01, yoma-005b-s02), independently reconstructed from rawHebrewLines and relevantRashi without trusting existing enrichment.
evidence.majorFindings: dafLevel.summary and s01's display/learning/argumentFlow narrative wrongly present the baraita (lines 5-9) as a direct continuation of the inauguration-passage indispensability bridge-building (steps 1-4, Lev. 8:35). Independently re-verified against relevantRashi on line 5: Rashi states explicitly this baraita's phrases are 'not that same verse belonging to the inauguration passage... but rather [the one] regarding the eighth day' (Lev. 10:12ff, the Nadav-and-Avihu aftermath). The shared 'ki chen tzuviti' wording is a coincidental phrase-match, not a substantive continuation. The dafLevel glossary's Aninus entry compounds this by stating the inauguration itself occurred while Nadav and Avihu had just died, when in fact they died on the eighth day, immediately after the inauguration concluded.
mediumFindings: s01 argumentFlow step-06 conflates two separate derivation mechanisms: trousers via the inclusive 've-zeh hadavar' vav, and the tenth-ephah via a distinct gezerah shavah on 'zeh'/'zeh' to Lev. 6:13 (already correctly separated in step-07). Text incorrectly implies both derive from the same mechanism.

dafLevel glossary's gezerah shavah entry omits the 'yeteira' (redundant repetition) requirement that licenses the petach analogy, confirmed present in Rashi's own gloss on line 2 ('redundantly, and likewise in the performance').
s01 lineRange.endVilnaLine declared 15, but step-08's own proof-text and conclusion run through line 18 ('ת''ל ויאמר משה אל העדה זה הדבר אשר צוה ה' אפילו דיבור מעכב'), an unaccounted boundary gap.

s02 argumentFlow step-03 telegraphs Abaye's belt-only narrowing ('(for the belt)') before the Gemara itself supplies it at step-04; at that point in the raw text (lines 22-25) the R. Chiyya's-sons/R. Yochanan dispute is stated in fully general terms.
minorFindings: s01/s02 topicTags contain capitalized non-slug values ('Leviticus', 'Moses', 'Abaye') violating the lowercase-hyphen-ASCII-slug contract.
s01/s02 requiresUnderstanding hold prose sentences instead of sugya ids, violating the contract (prose belongs in prerequisiteKnowledge).
s01/s02 visualizableElements use legacy 'description' key instead of the canonical required 'item' field.
noDefectsConfirmed: No cross-sugya lineId citations (all sourceRefs resolve within their own sugya's segment map).
s02's finalRuling correctly null; the belt-sequence stub is correctly framed as open, not resolved, with Rashi's own note confirming the answer continues on 6a.
Verse attributions in s02 step-05 (Lev. 8:7/8:13, Exod. 29:9) match Rashi's citations exactly.

evidence.reconstruction: Independent second-pass review, mutually-blind from the round-1 repair context (a6749807a314bfcfe). Reconstructed the whole daf from rawHebrewLines and relevantRashi: (1-4) three Amoraic bridges from Exodus-inauguration kachah to Leviticus requirements (petach-petach gezerah shavah, mishmeret-Hashem inclusivity, ki-chen-tzuviti warrant); (5-9) the eighth-day baraita distinguishing three near-identical phrases; (9-15) trousers and tenth-of-ephah derivations plus R. Yochanan's mikra-parasha point; (19-34) the dressing-order question, Abaye's belt-only narrowing, verse-proofs, and the unresolved challenge cut off mid-word at line 34.
evidence.attributionCheck: Verified against Rashi line by line: petach redundancy, mishmeret-Hashem inclusivity, the three ki-chen phrases' distinct referents, trousers/tenth-of-ephah sourcing, Abaye's belt-only narrowing, the verse-proofs and the reversed challenge. All match.
evidence.boundaryAndSourceRefCheck: Every argumentFlow step's lineId is one of its own sugya's sourceSegmentMap mintedLineIds, and every vilnaLine falls within that segment's declared containment range. No cross-sugya or cross-daf leakage; nothing from 6a is imported.
evidence.fabricationCheck: No fabrication found. The davar/dibbur gloss for R. Yochanan's derivation is directly supported by the Gemara's own adjacent wording (apilu dibbur me'akev), not invented.
evidence.closureCheck: finalRuling is null for both sugyot; s02's learning.resolution explicitly states the resolution is left for 6a. No misattributed closure.
evidence.majorFindingReverification: The line 5-9 baraita is correctly framed throughout (dafLevel.summary, s01 shortSummary/whats, step-05, note field) as belonging to the eighth-day/Nadav-Avihu passage (Lev. 10), appended only for shared ki-chen-tzuviti wording with Rav Ashi's proof, matching Rashi's own comment on line 5 verbatim. Trousers and tenth-of-ephah are correctly presented as two distinct mechanisms, matching Rashi's bishlama/ela structure. s02 step-03 describes the initial dispute with no premature mention of the belt; step-04 (Abaye) is where the belt-only scope is first introduced.
evidence.overallVerdict: No defects found in display, learning, argumentFlow, misconceptions, quizSeeds, glossary, or topicTags fields for either sugya.

reviewEvidence.summary: Comprehensive fresh reviewer cross-checked s01 against Sefaria's William Davidson Edition (fetched live, segments Yoma.6a.1-3). Found one sourceRef mis-citation.

defectFound.problem: Per the sugya's own lines[] segment map, l01 (vilnaLine 1) maps to Sefaria Yoma.6a.1, and l02 (vilnaLine 2) maps to Yoma.6a.2. Step-01's content (Position 1/'together's full answer: the belts are not the same, kilaim vs. plain linen, per Exodus 39:29) is entirely Sefaria segment Yoma.6a.1 -- which the Davidson translation confirms runs as one continuous paragraph including the material specifics, ending 'And still one can say that Aaron and his sons were dressed simultaneously.' Yoma.6a.2 is a DIFFERENT exchange (the challenge to Position 2 plus Position 2's own answer, already correctly cited by step-02). A prior round had moved this citation from l01 to l02 based on a naive reading of where the Vilna print's 'lo...zeh hu' sentence break falls, but the authoritative Sefaria-segment-to-lines[]-entry mapping this whole corpus is built on shows the full material-difference content belongs to segment 1 (l01), not segment 2 (l02).
defectFound.fix: sourceRef corrected to lineId yoma-006a-l01, vilnaLine 1.

evidence.summary: Sixth fresh reviewer, instructed to verify every sourceRef by fetching the actual Sefaria segment content live rather than eyeballing raw Vilna line-breaks. Confirmed s01 and s02 fully clean (all sourceRefs, factual content, and contract fields verified against fetched Sefaria segments Yoma.6a.1-6). Confirmed s03's substantive content clean (all steps verified against Yoma.6a.7-15 and 6b.1, including the daf's correct mid-sentence cutoff).

s03OneFlaggedPointInvestigatedAndRejecte.reviewerClaim: sourceSegmentMap's vilnaLine for the Yoma.6a.13 entry (mintedLineId l30) should be 31, not 30, based on live word-count analysis of the vocalized Sefaria Hebrew.
s03OneFlaggedPointInvestigatedAndRejecte.independentVerification: Checked directly against modules/yoma/source_store.js (the actual protected raw source this corpus is built from), lines 1072-1120: the sugya's own canonical lines[] array explicitly assigns vilna_line:28 to the grouped quotation spanning the baraita-1 citation through its final word ('lo'), and vilna_line:30 to the following 'nidah vechol de'atei meribuya' rejection clause -- vilna_line 29 is deliberately skipped by design, since the grouped 28-entry already subsumes that physical print line's content. Running build_learning_data.py after attempting the reviewer's suggested change (30->31) produced a hard validation error: 'vilna_line mismatch source=30 enrichment=31', confirming source_store.js's vilna_line:30 is the authoritative, protected value this corpus's own build pipeline enforces. The reviewer's live Sefaria word-count check does not account for this repo's own (looser, gap-tolerant) vilna_line assignment convention.
s03OneFlaggedPointInvestigatedAndRejecte.resolution: Reverted the attempted change. yoma-006a-l30's vilnaLine remains 30, matching the protected source_store.js data. No actual defect in s03's current (round 6) content.

evidence.otherChecksConfirmedClean: finalRuling, topicTags, requiresUnderstanding contract compliance verified for all three sugyot. No fabricated argumentFlow, no false resolution claims.

fieldInventory.note: answer: lines 1-2 (Position 1, 'together') answers why the implementation verses don't prove sequence - they teach material difference.
answer: line 2 (Position 2, 'Aaron first') answers the challenge from 've-chagarta otam' - the belts are identical.
question: lines 6-7 pose why two verses are needed if the belts are identical, and whether simultaneous girding is even possible.
resolution: lines 6-7 resolve both questions - the verses prove sequence, and 'bvat achat' means one uninterrupted operation, not literal simultaneity.
intermediate: requires tracking two coupled positions where the answer to a material question determines the answer to a sequence question.
textual: assigning command vs. implementation verses distinct teaching roles is a close-textual hermeneutical move.

reviewEvidence.summary: Comprehensive fresh reviewer cross-checked s03 against Sefaria's William Davidson Edition (fetched live, segments Yoma.6a.12-16 and 6b.1). Confirmed round 4's content correction (baraita 1 rejected via ribbuy, not left open) as substantively accurate -- 'Good repair.' Found three sourceRef/segment-map citation defects, all mechanical, none semantic.

defectsFound.problem: Per the sugya's own lines[] map, l31 -> Sefaria Yoma.6a.14 (baraita 2's citation, already correctly used by step-08), not the ribbuy-rejection content. The ribbuy-rejection (verified live: 'The Gemara rejects that proof because the term menstruating woman in that baraita includes...everyone whose inclusion...is derived from her status') is Sefaria Yoma.6a.13, which the lines[] map assigns to l30.
defectsFound.fix: sourceRef corrected to lineId yoma-006a-l30, vilnaLine 30.

defectsFound.before: sourceRef lineId yoma-006a-l33, vilnaLine 33; text conflated content from two distinct Sefaria segments
defectsFound.problem: Step-09's 'duration, not timing' deflection is part of Sefaria Yoma.6a.14 (the same long segment as step-08's baraita-2 citation), which maps to l31, not l33. Step-09's text had also absorbed a clause ('the Torah explicitly states both impurity durations') that actually belongs to the DIFFERENT, later Sefaria segment 6a.15 (step-10's rightful content), creating redundancy between step-09 and step-10.
defectsFound.fix: sourceRef corrected to lineId yoma-006a-l31, vilnaLine 31 (same segment as step-08). Text trimmed to only the duration-vs-timing deflection with its baal-keri/bo'el-niddah examples, removing the misplaced 'Torah explicitly states' clause.

defectsFound.before: step-10 cited lineId yoma-006a-l35, vilnaLine 35; s03.lines[] listed vilnaLine 35 -> sefariaRef 'Yoma.6a.16'
defectsFound.problem: Confirmed live via the Sefaria API: 'Yoma.6a.16' does not exist (daf 6a has only 15 segments; querying it returns 'We have no text for Yoma 6a:16'). The word at vilnaLine 35 ('ela') is actually the opening word of Sefaria Yoma.6b.1 ('Rather, must it not be that the baraita is equating them with regard to their immersion...'), confirmed live. Step-10's own content (the 'why teach duration if explicit' follow-up question) is Sefaria Yoma.6a.15, which the lines[] map correctly assigns to l33 (vilnaLine 33) -- a prior round had moved step-10's citation away from this correct value to the erroneous l35.
defectsFound.fix: step-10's sourceRef corrected back to lineId yoma-006a-l33, vilnaLine 33. The sugya's own lines[] entry for vilnaLine 35 corrected from the invalid 'Yoma.6a.16' to 'Yoma.6b.1', matching the confirmed live Sefaria structure.

reviewEvidence.confirmedAccurate: The substantive content correction from round 4 (baraita 1's ribbuy clause is the Gemara's REJECTION of the naive day-only inference, testing Rav Shimi's night-hypothesis, not an unanswered objection to R. Zeira) is confirmed correct against the live Davidson translation and required no further change. R. Zeira's day-conclusion, Rav Shimi's seven-vs-eight-days mechanism, and the daf's mid-sentence ending are all independently reconfirmed accurate.

evidence.summary: Sixth fresh reviewer, instructed to verify every sourceRef by fetching the actual Sefaria segment content live rather than eyeballing raw Vilna line-breaks. Confirmed s01 and s02 fully clean (all sourceRefs, factual content, and contract fields verified against fetched Sefaria segments Yoma.6a.1-6). Confirmed s03's substantive content clean (all steps verified against Yoma.6a.7-15 and 6b.1, including the daf's correct mid-sentence cutoff).

s03OneFlaggedPointInvestigatedAndRejecte.reviewerClaim: sourceSegmentMap's vilnaLine for the Yoma.6a.13 entry (mintedLineId l30) should be 31, not 30, based on live word-count analysis of the vocalized Sefaria Hebrew.
s03OneFlaggedPointInvestigatedAndRejecte.independentVerification: Checked directly against modules/yoma/source_store.js (the actual protected raw source this corpus is built from), lines 1072-1120: the sugya's own canonical lines[] array explicitly assigns vilna_line:28 to the grouped quotation spanning the baraita-1 citation through its final word ('lo'), and vilna_line:30 to the following 'nidah vechol de'atei meribuya' rejection clause -- vilna_line 29 is deliberately skipped by design, since the grouped 28-entry already subsumes that physical print line's content. Running build_learning_data.py after attempting the reviewer's suggested change (30->31) produced a hard validation error: 'vilna_line mismatch source=30 enrichment=31', confirming source_store.js's vilna_line:30 is the authoritative, protected value this corpus's own build pipeline enforces. The reviewer's live Sefaria word-count check does not account for this repo's own (looser, gap-tolerant) vilna_line assignment convention.
s03OneFlaggedPointInvestigatedAndRejecte.resolution: Reverted the attempted change. yoma-006a-l30's vilnaLine remains 30, matching the protected source_store.js data. No actual defect in s03's current (round 6) content.

evidence.otherChecksConfirmedClean: finalRuling, topicTags, requiresUnderstanding contract compliance verified for all three sugyot. No fabricated argumentFlow, no false resolution claims.

evidence.summary: Fresh, isolated Source Auditor first-pass audit of Yoma 6b (yoma-006b-s01, yoma-006b-s02), independently reconstructed from rawHebrewLines and relevantRashi, with every objection/resolution step cross-checked against Sefaria's live API. Confirmed defects, now repaired.
majorFindings: dafLevel.summary's final sentence misstated the beit-av dispute's scope: verified against Sefaria Yoma.6b.7 that everyone agrees a MIXED beit av (some pure, some impure) simply uses its pure priests -- no dispute there. The dispute is narrower: whether to summon from a DIFFERENT beit av when the entire on-duty unit is impure. dafLevel's own glossary and s02's own shortSummary already had this right, making the summary's own final sentence an internal inconsistency. Corrected.

s01 argumentFlow step-01 fabricated 'bo'el niddah is an av hatumah like tamei meit', inverting the actual teaching: verified against Sefaria Yoma.6b.2, bo'el niddah's mishkav/moshav transmission is explicitly the MILD (rishon le-tumah, food/drink only) form, contrasted with tamei meit's more severe direct-contact transmission -- the opposite of 'av hatumah'. Step-01 also cited lineId l01a (Sefaria Yoma.6b.1, confirmed to be only the reopened question, not a resolution) for content that is actually the resolution (Sefaria Yoma.6b.2, l01b, already correctly used by step-02), and mislabeled itself as resolving 6a's dangling immersion-timing question when the actual resolution is step-03 (R. Chiyya's baraita). Rewrote step-01 to accurately state the duration-not-timing resolution with correct dual sourceRefs (l01a for the reopened question, l01b for the answer), removing the redundant/fabricated mishkav-moshav restatement now that step-02 already covers it accurately. Also removed the same 'av hatumah' fabrication from visualizableElements[1]'s description.
mediumFindings: s01 display.shortSummary/whats causally mislinked the mishkav/moshav teaching to R. Chiyya's baraita ('this also confirms, incidentally...' / 'the baraita also triggers...'), when in the actual text the mishkav/moshav point is established BEFORE R. Chiyya's baraita is even cited, via a separate exegetical passage. Reworded to present the two proofs (duration/mishkav-moshav resolution, then R. Chiyya's separate immersion-timing refutation) as sequential and independent.

Neither dafLevel.summary nor any s01 field named whose position R. Chiyya's baraita refutes: verified against Sefaria Yoma.6b.3 ('a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rav Shimi from Neharde'a'). Added explicit naming of Rav Shimi across dafLevel.summary, display fields, and learning.ahaMoment.

s01.lineRange.endVilnaLine (11) left Ravina's own core reasoning (lines 12-13, already correctly covered by step-06's existing l11 segment citation per the containment convention) outside the sugya's declared boundary. Widened to 13.
minorFindings: s01/s02 topicTags contained capitalized non-slug values (Kohen-Gadol, Yom-Kippur, Temple-service, Rav-Nachman, Rav-Sheshet) violating the lowercase-hyphen-ASCII-slug contract.

s01/s02 requiresUnderstanding held prose instead of sugya ids, with no prerequisiteKnowledge field present anywhere to receive it. s01's 'bo'el niddah immersion timing established in 6a' resolved to a genuine sugya id, yoma-006a-s03.
s01/s02 visualizableElements used the legacy 'description' key across all 5 entries instead of the canonical required 'item' field.
noDefectsConfirmed: s02's full argumentFlow (formal dispute statement, same-beit-av scope restriction, Rav Nachman's ruling, Rav Sheshet's ruling, the ikka de'amrei second version) checked line-by-line against Sefaria and found accurate.
No cross-sugya lineId citations found anywhere on the daf.
s02's daf-boundary handling of the genuine mid-word cutoff at line 24 (confirmed by Rashi's own note) is correctly left open with no false closure.

evidence.summary: Independent second-pass review, mutually-blind from the round-1 repair context (a2dc186e2f7440258). Cross-checked every objection/rejection/resolution step against Sefaria's live API. Confirmed: bo'el niddah's mishkav/moshav transmission is correctly described as the mild rishon-le-tumah form (Sefaria Yoma.6b.2), not av hatumah; 6a's dangling immersion-timing question is correctly resolved on 6b, not claimed resolved on 6a; all sourceRefs lineId/vilnaLine pairs resolve correctly within their declared segment ranges; finalRuling, topicTags, and requiresUnderstanding all contract-compliant. evidence.method: Read all 32 authoritative Hebrew/Aramaic lines and the bundled Rashi for the full physical daf before auditing the enrichment. Checked all three declared sugyot, the whole-daf summary, speaker attribution, source references, physical cutoff, and stale or imported-next-daf claims.
independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-21 complete the separation and sprinkling discussion. Day 4 can never be a useful day-3 sprinkling because no new impurity can arise after separation. It can chronologically coincide with day 7 only for impurity beginning before separation, but then the required day-3 sprinkling was missed before separation, so the day-7 sprinkling accomplishes nothing. Sprinkling is omitted on Shabbat as a shvut. The Yom Kippur priest's start is calendar-fixed; the para priest's start is scheduled so day 4 falls on Shabbat.

Lines 21-28 explain Balvati and Parhedrin. In the later Second Temple period the purchased office changed hands yearly; each new High Priest demolished the chamber and rebuilt it more beautifully under his own name. The yearly rebuilding and replacement grounds the comparison to annually replaced parhedrin.

Lines 29-32 state the bakers' demai rule. Per Rashi, terumat maaser and challah are given, maaser rishon and maaser ani are separated but not given, and the baker's special leniency is not separating or redeeming maaser sheni. The Gemara begins its justification and the daf ends after 'because', continuing on 9a.

dafBoundary.notes: The physical daf ends after the opening word 'because' in the terumah gedolah justification. No content from 9a may be imported to complete it.

findings: The quiz answer falsely says day 4 cannot chronologically be day 7. It can, but the sprinkling is ineffective because the matching day-3 sprinkling was missed before separation.
The learning blocker falsely says weekday day-4 sprinkling may be substantively needed in some years. It is never needed, though the all-days-except-Shabbat schedule still performs it on a weekday.
Related summary, hint, and argument-flow wording must express the same exact logic and describe the Shabbat rule as a rabbinic prohibition or shvut.
coreTension says annual appointees never stayed long enough to build, directly contradicting Rashi: every incoming High Priest demolished and rebuilt the chamber more beautifully.
Dark-humor, sardonic-renaming, and form-of-mourning claims exceed the source and must be replaced by the grounded purchased-office, yearly-replacement account.
The local title and display prose improperly fold the bakers unit into a sugya whose line range ends before it.
finalRuling says no other tithe separation is required, contradicting Rashi's explicit separation without giving of maaser rishon and maaser ani.
The special baker leniency must be identified as not separating or redeeming maaser sheni, while preserving the incomplete explanation at the 8b cutoff.

All conclusions below were derived solely from authoritativeHebrewLines and relevantRashi in the packet, reconstructed independently before any certification registry file was opened.
evidence.independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-21: baraita distinguishes the YK kohen gadol's separation (for holiness/kedusha, entering the Divine Presence's camp - Rashi confirms via 'to enter the camp of the Shechina' - other priests may touch him) from the para-aduma priest's separation (for purity/tahara, to preempt Sadducean claims - Rashi confirms via 'to drive the notion from the heart of the Sadducees' - other priests may not touch him). Gemara: the baraita follows R. Meir or R. Yosei, not R. Chanina Segan HaKohanim (who would add a second difference, the sprinkling schedule, per 8a). R. Yosei b'R. Chanina then challenges the Mishnah's schedule: days 1-3 and 5-7 are each plausible as a real 3rd or 7th day of some undetected tumah, but day 4 can be neither (no new tumah can arise once separation/supervision has begun, ruling out a real day-3; and a chronological day-7 coincidence would require a day-3 sprinkling that fell before separation began and so was never done - a 7th without a 3rd accomplishes nothing) - so why is day 4 sprinkled at all? The 'ולטעמיך...לבר מרביעי' passage (lines 10-14) presses this by analogy to the already-accepted fact that 'all seven' already tolerates an exception (hazaah is a shvut and does not override Shabbat), so a further exception for day 4 is coherent. Rava then resolves practically (confirmed by Rashi's gloss on 'וכל אימת דמתרמי...מפרשינן ליה', which states his sprinkling 'turns out to be void for two days' when day 4 misses Shabbat, vs. Rashi's gloss on 'רביעי בשבת' stating interruption 'for only one day' when engineered onto Shabbat): the YK kohen gadol's separation start (3 Tishrei) is calendar-fixed, so day 4 is sprinkled on ordinary weekdays regardless of futility, and only accidentally skipped when it lands on Shabbat; the para priest's start date is our choice, so we begin his separation on the 4th day of the week (Wednesday) so day 4 always lands on Shabbat and the futile sprinkling is always the one already excluded by the shvut rule. Lines 21-28: Mishnah cue 'ללשכת פרהדרין' opens a new unit. R. Yehuda's baraita: the chamber was originally called Lishkat Balvati (Rashi: through the era of Shimon HaTzaddik). Once (Second Temple) priests paid money for the office (Rashi: to the Hasmonean kings) and were wicked and did not complete their year (Rashi, explicit), each newly appointed priest would demolish the chamber and rebuild a finer one to bear his own name (Rashi, explicit, glossing 'ומחליפין אותה'), so it was renamed Lishkat Parhedrin after the Persian parhedrin who were likewise replaced every twelve months. Lines 29-32: Mishnah cue 'תנן התם' opens the bakers unit: the baraita states the Sages did not obligate bakers to separate anything from demai grain except terumat maaser and challah. Rashi's gloss, read against the general demai rule (terumat maaser given to a kohen; maaser rishon/maaser ani separated but withheld per the general safek-demai rule that applies to everyone, not a baker-specific carveout; maaser sheni must ordinarily be brought to Jerusalem or redeemed), isolates the bakers' own distinctive leniency as exemption from the maaser-sheni Jerusalem/redemption step, because as chaverim selling continuously that step is impractical for them - consistent with the 9a continuation (Yochanan Kohen Gadol/Ulla) this sugya is en route to. The Gemara begins justifying the rule tier by tier - 'בשלמא תרומה גדולה לא דתניא לפי...' - and is cut off after the single word 'לפי' (because) at the daf's physical end; Rashi's own note on this word ('the comment is completed on 9a') confirms the cutoff is a physical daf boundary, not a content gap.
evidence.boundaryNotes: Three topic units, each opened by an explicit Mishnah-citation cue in the source ('ללשכת פרהדרין וכו'' at line 21; 'תנן התם' at line 29) or by a baraita continuing directly from 8a's dispute (lines 1-21). Sugya 1 (1-21) and sugya 2 (21-28) share line 21 because that single line physically contains both the end of Rava's ruling and the start of the next Mishnah lemma - correct handling of a mid-line topic transition, not an error. Sugya 3 (29-32) ends at the daf's literal physical boundary (mid-word, 'לפי'), matching Rashi's explicit note that the comment concludes on 9a. No sugya needed on this daf is missing and no declared range crosses a real topic boundary.
evidence.dafSummaryNotes: All three paragraphs of currentDafSummary were checked line-by-line against authoritativeHebrewLines and relevantRashi. Attribution of holiness/touchable to the YK kohen gadol and purity/untouchable to the para priest is confirmed by Rashi's explicit gloss (camp of the Shechina vs. Sadducee polemic). The day-4 argument, the shvut/Shabbat exception, and Rava's calendar-vs-our-control distinction are confirmed, including the quantitative detail (not stated in the summary but not contradicted by it) that Rashi quantifies the YK kohen gadol's non-Shabbat case as two void/interrupted days vs. one for the scheduled para priest. Lishkat Parhedrin history (money for office, wicked/short tenures, physical demolition and rebuilding per new appointee, analogy to rotating Persian parhedrin) is confirmed verbatim by Rashi's explicit gloss on 'מחליפין אותה'. The bakers' rule and the mid-word 'לפי' cutoff with Rashi's 9a continuation note are confirmed exactly.

independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-21 complete the separation and sprinkling discussion. Day 4 can never be a useful day-3 sprinkling because no new impurity can arise after separation. It can chronologically coincide with day 7 only for impurity beginning before separation, but then the required day-3 sprinkling was missed before separation, so the day-7 sprinkling accomplishes nothing. Sprinkling is omitted on Shabbat as a shvut. The Yom Kippur priest's start is calendar-fixed; the para priest's start is scheduled so day 4 falls on Shabbat.

Lines 21-28 explain Balvati and Parhedrin. In the later Second Temple period the purchased office changed hands yearly; each new High Priest demolished the chamber and rebuilt it more beautifully under his own name. The yearly rebuilding and replacement grounds the comparison to annually replaced parhedrin.

Lines 29-32 state the bakers' demai rule. Per Rashi, terumat maaser and challah are given, maaser rishon and maaser ani are separated but not given, and the baker's special leniency is not separating or redeeming maaser sheni. The Gemara begins its justification and the daf ends after 'because', continuing on 9a.

dafBoundary.notes: The physical daf ends after the opening word 'because' in the terumah gedolah justification. No content from 9a may be imported to complete it.

findings: The quiz answer falsely says day 4 cannot chronologically be day 7. It can, but the sprinkling is ineffective because the matching day-3 sprinkling was missed before separation.
The learning blocker falsely says weekday day-4 sprinkling may be substantively needed in some years. It is never needed, though the all-days-except-Shabbat schedule still performs it on a weekday.
Related summary, hint, and argument-flow wording must express the same exact logic and describe the Shabbat rule as a rabbinic prohibition or shvut.
coreTension says annual appointees never stayed long enough to build, directly contradicting Rashi: every incoming High Priest demolished and rebuilt the chamber more beautifully.
Dark-humor, sardonic-renaming, and form-of-mourning claims exceed the source and must be replaced by the grounded purchased-office, yearly-replacement account.
The local title and display prose improperly fold the bakers unit into a sugya whose line range ends before it.
finalRuling says no other tithe separation is required, contradicting Rashi's explicit separation without giving of maaser rishon and maaser ani.

evidence.independentSourceReconstruction: The daf proceeds from Rava's Wednesday-start solution for the para priest versus the calendar-fixed Yom Kippur High Priest, through R. Yehuda's account of Lishkat Balvati becoming Lishkat Parhedrin as purchased High Priests turned over annually, and ends mid-discussion with the terumat-maaser and challah versus other tithe obligations, cut off at the word lefi and continuing on 9a.

perSugya.notes: Boundary vilna 1-21, the kman exclusion of R. Chanina Segan HaKohanim, R. Yosei b. R. Chanina's challenge, and Rava's Wednesday-start scheduling solution all match the source. The day-4/day-7 coincidence point and preceding day-3 sprinkling match the linked Rashi.

Boundary vilna 21-28, R. Yehuda's baraita attribution, the Lishkat Balvati to Lishkat Parhedrin history, purchased office, annual turnover, rebuilding, and Shimon HaTzaddik detail match the linked Rashi. Splitting the continuous baraita into R. Yehuda and Baraita speakers is content-accurate and stylistic only.

Boundary vilna 29-32 ends at the cut-off word lefi, with Rashi explicitly noting continuation on 9a. The terumat-maaser and challah given, maaser-rishon and ani separated but not given, and maaser-sheni exemption structure matches Rashi.

independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-21 complete the separation and sprinkling discussion. Day 4 can never be a useful day-3 sprinkling because no new impurity can arise after separation. It can chronologically coincide with day 7 only for impurity beginning before separation, but then the required day-3 sprinkling was missed before separation, so the day-7 sprinkling accomplishes nothing. Sprinkling is omitted on Shabbat as a shvut. The Yom Kippur priest's start is calendar-fixed; the para priest's start is scheduled so day 4 falls on Shabbat.

Lines 21-28 explain Balvati and Parhedrin. In the later Second Temple period the purchased office changed hands yearly; each new High Priest demolished the chamber and rebuilt it more beautifully under his own name. The yearly rebuilding and replacement grounds the comparison to annually replaced parhedrin.

Lines 29-32 state the bakers' demai rule. Per Rashi, terumat maaser and challah are given, maaser rishon and maaser ani are separated but not given, and the baker's special leniency is not separating or redeeming maaser sheni. The Gemara begins its justification and the daf ends after 'because', continuing on 9a.

dafBoundary.notes: The physical daf ends after the opening word 'because' in the terumah gedolah justification. No content from 9a may be imported to complete it.

findings: The quiz answer falsely says day 4 cannot chronologically be day 7. It can, but the sprinkling is ineffective because the matching day-3 sprinkling was missed before separation.
The learning blocker falsely says weekday day-4 sprinkling may be substantively needed in some years. It is never needed, though the all-days-except-Shabbat schedule still performs it on a weekday.
Related summary, hint, and argument-flow wording must express the same exact logic and describe the Shabbat rule as a rabbinic prohibition or shvut.
coreTension says annual appointees never stayed long enough to build, directly contradicting Rashi: every incoming High Priest demolished and rebuilt the chamber more beautifully.
Dark-humor, sardonic-renaming, and form-of-mourning claims exceed the source and must be replaced by the grounded purchased-office, yearly-replacement account.
The local title and display prose improperly fold the bakers unit into a sugya whose line range ends before it.
finalRuling says no other tithe separation is required, contradicting Rashi's explicit separation without giving of maaser rishon and maaser ani.
The special baker leniency must be identified as not separating or redeeming maaser sheni, while preserving the incomplete explanation at the 8b cutoff.

evidence.independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-21: baraita distinguishes the YK kohen gadol's separation (for holiness/kedusha, entering the Divine Presence's camp - Rashi confirms via 'to enter the camp of the Shechina' - other priests may touch him) from the para-aduma priest's separation (for purity/tahara, to preempt Sadducean claims - Rashi confirms via 'to drive the notion from the heart of the Sadducees' - other priests may not touch him). Gemara: the baraita follows R. Meir or R. Yosei, not R. Chanina Segan HaKohanim (who would add a second difference, the sprinkling schedule, per 8a). R. Yosei b'R. Chanina then challenges the Mishnah's schedule: days 1-3 and 5-7 are each plausible as a real 3rd or 7th day of some undetected tumah, but day 4 can be neither (no new tumah can arise once separation/supervision has begun, ruling out a real day-3; and a chronological day-7 coincidence would require a day-3 sprinkling that fell before separation began and so was never done - a 7th without a 3rd accomplishes nothing) - so why is day 4 sprinkled at all? The 'ולטעמיך...לבר מרביעי' passage (lines 10-14) presses this by analogy to the already-accepted fact that 'all seven' already tolerates an exception (hazaah is a shvut and does not override Shabbat), so a further exception for day 4 is coherent. Rava then resolves practically (confirmed by Rashi's gloss on 'וכל אימת דמתרמי...מפרשינן ליה', which states his sprinkling 'turns out to be void for two days' when day 4 misses Shabbat, vs. Rashi's gloss on 'רביעי בשבת' stating interruption 'for only one day' when engineered onto Shabbat): the YK kohen gadol's separation start (3 Tishrei) is calendar-fixed, so day 4 is sprinkled on ordinary weekdays regardless of futility, and only accidentally skipped when it lands on Shabbat; the para priest's start date is our choice, so we begin his separation on the 4th day of the week (Wednesday) so day 4 always lands on Shabbat and the futile sprinkling is always the one already excluded by the shvut rule. Lines 21-28: Mishnah cue 'ללשכת פרהדרין' opens a new unit. R. Yehuda's baraita: the chamber was originally called Lishkat Balvati (Rashi: through the era of Shimon HaTzaddik). Once (Second Temple) priests paid money for the office (Rashi: to the Hasmonean kings) and were wicked and did not complete their year (Rashi, explicit), each newly appointed priest would demolish the chamber and rebuild a finer one to bear his own name (Rashi, explicit, glossing 'ומחליפין אותה'), so it was renamed Lishkat Parhedrin after the Persian parhedrin who were likewise replaced every twelve months. Lines 29-32: Mishnah cue 'תנן התם' opens the bakers unit: the baraita states the Sages did not obligate bakers to separate anything from demai grain except terumat maaser and challah. Rashi's gloss, read against the general demai rule (terumat maaser given to a kohen; maaser rishon/maaser ani separated but withheld per the general safek-demai rule that applies to everyone, not a baker-specific carveout; maaser sheni must ordinarily be brought to Jerusalem or redeemed), isolates the bakers' own distinctive leniency as exemption from the maaser-sheni Jerusalem/redemption step, because as chaverim selling continuously that step is impractical for them - consistent with the 9a continuation (Yochanan Kohen Gadol/Ulla) this sugya is en route to. sourceFlow.finding: The daf completes the demai/bakers discussion: terumah gedolah alone was reliably separated; maaser rishon and maaser ani remain governed by hamotzi me-chavero alav ha-ra'ayah; maaser sheni is separated and eaten in Jerusalem; Ulla explains the exemption of pressured bakers from an added burden.
The Gemara asks about parhedrin, then contrasts the First Temple's 410 years and 18 High Priests with the Second Temple's 420 years and more than 300 High Priests, most not completing a year.

R. Yochanan ben Torta attributes Shiloh's destruction to giluy arayot and bizayon kodashim; the verse concerning Eli's sons is cited; R. Shmuel bar Nachmani in R. Yochanan's name rejects a literal reading, and the daf stops at 'מתוך ששהו' before identifying what was delayed.

evidence.sourceReadDeclaration: Read authoritative Hebrew Vilna lines 1-50 in order before inspecting the candidate enrichment.
evidence.independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-9 complete the Eli-sons discussion. Lines 10-23 prove the First Temple's three sins. Lines 24-31 contrast Second Temple sinat chinam and return to the First Temple generation's reliance on God and three decrees. Lines 32-35 restrict the cited First Temple hatred to the princes. Lines 35-39 correlate exposed sin with an exposed end and use the rebuilt Temple as evidence favoring the former generation. Lines 40-48 contain the Jordan rebuke, wall-door exposition, sasmagor, bat kol, and participant challenge. Lines 48-50 record R. Yochanan's substantive rebuttal that even a complete return would not have brought the Shechina to the Second Temple, followed by a proof cut off mid-argument.

defects: Remove the unsupported claim that both offenses served priestly personal interests; the bird-offering delay is described as arrogance or laxness.
Remove the invented communal-destruction-capacity explanation of sinat chinam's equivalence and the invented necessity mechanism linking retained trust to calibrated punishment.
Confine the teaching to the direct challenge and princes-only answer; do not claim social scope explains the exile endpoint.
Remove the invented repentance and rebuke mechanism.
Do not call the generational-merit exchange unresolved or the Temple evidence inconclusive; it is presented as evidence favoring the former generation.
Attach R. Yochanan's rejection to Reish Lakish's causal claim, not the participant objection.
Translate afilu as even if: even had all ascended, the Shechina would not have rested in the Second Temple; preserve the cut-off proof.

evidence.sourceReadDeclaration: Read authoritative Hebrew Vilna lines 1-50 in order before inspecting the candidate enrichment.
evidence.independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-9 complete the Eli-sons discussion. Lines 10-23 prove the First Temple's three sins. Lines 24-31 contrast Second Temple sinat chinam and return to the First Temple generation's reliance on God and three decrees. Lines 32-35 restrict the cited First Temple hatred to the princes. Lines 35-39 correlate exposed sin with an exposed end and use the rebuilt Temple as evidence favoring the former generation. Lines 40-48 contain the Jordan rebuke, wall-door exposition, sasmagor, bat kol, and participant challenge. Lines 48-50 record R. Yochanan's substantive rebuttal that even a complete return would not have brought the Shechina to the Second Temple, followed by a proof cut off mid-argument.

defects: Remove the unsupported claim that both offenses served priestly personal interests; the bird-offering delay is described as arrogance or laxness.
Remove the invented communal-destruction-capacity explanation of sinat chinam's equivalence and the invented necessity mechanism linking retained trust to calibrated punishment.
Confine the teaching to the direct challenge and princes-only answer; do not claim social scope explains the exile endpoint.
Remove the invented repentance and rebuke mechanism.
Do not call the generational-merit exchange unresolved or the Temple evidence inconclusive; it is presented as evidence favoring the former generation.
Attach R. Yochanan's rejection to Reish Lakish's causal claim, not the participant objection.
Translate afilu as even if: even had all ascended, the Shechina would not have rested in the Second Temple; preserve the cut-off proof.

Elazar's answer across lines 39-40; 40-50 give the Jordan rebuke and R. Yochanan's contrary Shechina argument, whose proof continues on 10a.

evidence.sourceReadDeclaration: Read authoritative Hebrew Vilna lines 1-50 in order before inspecting the candidate enrichment.
evidence.independentSourceReconstruction: Lines 1-9 complete the Eli-sons discussion. Lines 10-23 prove the First Temple's three sins. Lines 24-31 contrast Second Temple sinat chinam and return to the First Temple generation's reliance on God and three decrees. Lines 32-35 restrict the cited First Temple hatred to the princes. Lines 35-39 correlate exposed sin with an exposed end and use the rebuilt Temple as evidence favoring the former generation. Lines 40-48 contain the Jordan rebuke, wall-door exposition, sasmagor, bat kol, and participant challenge. Lines 48-50 record R. Yochanan's substantive rebuttal that even a complete return would not have brought the Shechina to the Second Temple, followed by a proof cut off mid-argument.

defects: Remove the unsupported claim that both offenses served priestly personal interests; the bird-offering delay is described as arrogance or laxness.
Remove the invented communal-destruction-capacity explanation of sinat chinam's equivalence and the invented necessity mechanism linking retained trust to calibrated punishment.
Confine the teaching to the direct challenge and princes-only answer; do not claim social scope explains the exile endpoint.
Remove the invented repentance and rebuke mechanism.
Do not call the generational-merit exchange unresolved or the Temple evidence inconclusive; it is presented as evidence favoring the former generation.
Attach R. Yochanan's rejection to Reish Lakish's causal claim, not the participant objection.
Translate afilu as even if: even had all ascended, the Shechina would not have rested in the Second Temple; preserve the cut-off proof.

Lines 35-39 correlate exposed sin with an exposed end and use the rebuilt Temple as evidence favoring the former generation. Lines 40-48 contain the Jordan rebuke, wall-door exposition, sasmagor, bat kol, and participant challenge. Lines 48-50 record R. Yochanan's substantive rebuttal that even a complete return would not have brought the Shechina to the Second Temple, followed by a proof cut off mid-argument.

defects: Remove the unsupported claim that both offenses served priestly personal interests; the bird-offering delay is described as arrogance or laxness.
Remove the invented communal-destruction-capacity explanation of sinat chinam's equivalence and the invented necessity mechanism linking retained trust to calibrated punishment.
Confine the teaching to the direct challenge and princes-only answer; do not claim social scope explains the exile endpoint.
Remove the invented repentance and rebuke mechanism.
Do not call the generational-merit exchange unresolved or the Temple evidence inconclusive; it is presented as evidence favoring the former generation.
Attach R. Yochanan's rejection to Reish Lakish's causal claim, not the participant objection.
Translate afilu as even if: even had all ascended, the Shechina would not have rested in the Second Temple; preserve the cut-off proof.

independentWholeDafFlow: Lines 1-28 complete the Yefet/Shem statement, identify biblical nations and places, establish Tiras as Persia, and interpret Achiman, Sheshai and Talmai.

Lines 41-48 begin the Parhedrin-mezuza discussion and end mid-response at 'dilma'.

dafLevelReview.summary: CONFIRMED: the page summary accurately preserves the three topic blocks and explicitly marks the final mezuza argument unresolved.
dafLevelReview.glossary: CONFIRMED: the daf glossary entries were checked and no defect affecting this candidate was found.

boundaryAndCoordinateReview.verdict: REJECTED: the topic boundary itself is sound, but argumentFlow.step-05 cites line 15 for the Tiras-to-Persia lineage conclusion even though line 15 begins Kalneh/Asshur material; the supporting source is lines 3-9.

defects.currentClaim: Rav Yosef continues identifying all the listed Genesis 10 places, including Bavel, Erech, Akkad, Kalneh, Nineveh, Rechovot Ir, Kalach and Resen.
defects.sourceActuallySupports: Rav Yosef is expressly attributed at lines 10 and 16 only for the Sakistan identification and Asshur=Silek. The intervening and following city identifications are anonymous Gemara material.
defects.requiredCorrection: Do not attribute the entire step to Rav Yosef; split the attributed teachings from the anonymous identifications or use an accurate mixed attribution.

defects.currentClaim: The Tiras/Persia/Yefet conclusion is anchored to Vilna line 15.
defects.sourceActuallySupports: Line 15 concerns Kalneh and the beginning of the Asshur passage. Tiras is listed as Yefet's son and identified as Persia at lines 3-9.
defects.requiredCorrection: Point this conclusion to an in-range source anchor covering lines 3-9.

defects.currentClaim: Every nation identification has prophetic stakes and every mapped nation determines which prophecies apply or who wins the end game.
defects.sourceActuallySupports: The daf uses Tiras=Persia in the ensuing prophecy discussion. It does not assign prophetic stakes to every other identification in the list.
defects.requiredCorrection: Narrow the pedagogical claim to the demonstrated significance of the Persia/Tiras identification and avoid universalizing that function to every name.

defects.currentClaim: The two Rome-falls-to-Persia teachings are a 'majority view' opposed by Rav.

defects.requiredCorrection: Describe these as the two earlier teachings or the Rome-falls-to-Persia position, not as a majority view.

defects.currentClaim: Treating the passage as a historical prediction is a misconception; it is theological argument, not simple prediction.
defects.sourceActuallySupports: The repeated formula 'atida ... shetipol' explicitly predicts a future imperial outcome, supported by theological and exegetical reasoning. Calling historical prediction itself a misconception contradicts the passage's plain claim.
defects.requiredCorrection: If retaining the pedagogical point, say the prediction is argued through prophetic/theological reasoning rather than denying that it is a prediction.
